hints.content:
The basic function $\sin(x)$ intersects its midline at $(0,0)$ and has a maximum point at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},1\right)$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

Let's transform $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\blue{5\sin(2x-3\pi)-2}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, one).

hints.content:
The transformation from $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\green{\sin(2x)}$ is a horizontal shrink by a factor of $2$, so the maximum point's horizontal distance from the origin is shrunk from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\sin(2x)}$ to $\red{5\sin(2x)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $5$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over four, one).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, four). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, five).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{5\sin(2x)}$ to $\blue{5\sin(2x-3\pi)-2}$, which is equivalent to $5\sin{\large(}2(x-1.5\pi){\large)}-2$, is a translation to the right by $1.5\pi$ units and a translation downwards by $2$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the intersection point with the midline is now at $\left(1.5\pi,-2\right)$ and the maximum point is at $(1.75\pi,3)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at the midline at (one and one half pi, negative two) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (one and sevety five hundredths pi, three).

question.content:

*Note that one moveable point always defines an extremum point in the graph and the other point always defines a neighbouring intersection with the midline.*
